title: Effect of a Commercial Diosgenin-Standardized Yam Extract on the Biological Activity of C2C12 Cells and Endurance Performance in Endurance-Trained Individuals
summary:
The popularity of plant-based steroids for improving physical health and performance is steadily increasing. Such plant-based steroids include, amongst others, diosgenin (DIO), which is found mainly in fenugreek (4) or in yam roots (5), and ecdysterone (ECDY), which is found, amongst other sources, in spinach (28).
DIO, in particular, is believed to have biological activity and is therefore the most extensively studied component of fenugreek (Fuller and Stephens 2015). DIO is a steroidal saponin and belongs to the group of biologically active phytosteroids. It has a chemical structure almost identical to that of human steroids, with a hydroxyl group at the third beta position, a double bond at the 5-6 position and an R-configuration at position 25. Owing to this molecular structure, DIO possesses a wide range of properties for combating various diseases such as cancer, multiple sclerosis, diabetes, liver fibrosis and arthritis (20).
Furthermore, recent review articles point to possible anabolic and performance-enhancing effects (1, 7). Initial studies have demonstrated anabolic effects in C2C12 cells as well as hypertrophic effects on the gastrocnemius muscle in rats (16). These findings have been confirmed by recent studies conducted by our research group. Furthermore, additive anabolic effects were observed with ecdysterone in C2C12 cells ((15), 21C19EI).
